models.title: Bear put spread breakeven
models.summary: Breakeven underlying price for a put bear spread as the higher (long-put) strike minus the net cost of the spread.

relationship.locator: PDF: LM1 bear spreads, printed pp. 35-36 (PDF pp. 43-44), Exhibit 18 (buy NOV 16 put at 1.96, write NOV 15 put at 1.46): net cost 0.50 (maximum loss); breakeven 16-1.96+1.46 = 15.50
relationship.translation_notes: Decimals. XH > XL; pH > pL so the spread has positive cost.

models.title: Collar flat-region terminal profit
models.summary: Terminal profit of a collar in either flat region as the binding strike minus inception stock price minus net premium paid.

relationship.original_equation: Profit = X1 - S0 - p0 + c0 at/below the put strike; X2 - S0 - p0 + c0 at/above the call strike
relationship.locator: PDF: LM1 collars, printed p. 44 (PDF p. 52), Exhibits 23-24 (stock bought at 12, NOV 15 put at 1.46, NOV 17 call written at 1.44): flat-region profit X1-S0-p0+c0 = 15-12-1.46+1.44 = 2.98 at/below the put strike; X2-S0-p0+c0 = 17-12-1.46+1.44 = 4.98 at/above the call strike
relationship.translation_notes: Decimals. K is the binding strike (X1 floor region, X2 cap region); p0/c0 are put cost/call receipt.

variables.definition: Strike binding in the flat region (put strike X1 or call strike X2), in currency units
Stock purchase price, in currency units
Put premium paid, in currency units
Call premium received, in currency units
Terminal profit in the flat region, in currency units

assumptions: Long stock plus long put (X1) plus short call (X2), X2 > X1, same expiry; evaluated in a flat region.
limitations: Flat regions only; between the strikes profit rises one-for-one with the stock.
